items.label: Overview
items.content:
# NexGame Component

`NexGame` is a lightweight, performance-optimized custom HTML5 element (`<nex-game>`) designed to fetch, cache, and securely execute web games.

## Key Features
- Race-fetch strategy across multiple CDN nodes
- Aggressive Cache Storage caching (minimizes cellular data usage)
- Isolated, high-permission sandbox iframe execution
- Self-healing runtime with hot-reload capabilities

## Installation
```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/usenex/nex-js@f10e7a480b7d1d3b5af4b0e3066d8115f7f0c356/nex.min.js"></script>
```

items.label: Attributes
items.content:
# Component Attributes

The `<nex-game>` element supports the following attributes:

| Attribute | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alias` | `string` | Unique identifier name of the target game (e.g., `"fnaf"`) |
| `gid` | `string` | Unique session identifier for event mapping and instance deduplication |

## Example
```html
<nex-game alias="fnaf" gid="session-123"></nex-game>
```

items.label: Global API (window.nex)
items.content:
# Global API (`window.nex`)

The component exposes a reactive registry proxy attached to `window.nex[gid]`.

## Methods

### `on(eventName, callback)`
Registers an event listener for a specific lifecycle phase. Can be declared before the DOM element is instantiated.

**Parameters:**
- `eventName`: `"progress"` | `"ready"` | `"error"`
- `callback`: `(data: Object) => void`

**Example:**
```js
window.nex["session-123"].on("ready", () => {
  console.log("Game is ready!")
})
```

### `start()`
Triggers execution and rendering of the game inside the shadow DOM sandbox. If assets are still downloading, execution remains pending until the `"ready"` event fires.

**Example:**
```js
window.nex["session-123"].start()
```

items.label: progress
items.content:
# `progress` Event

Fired continuously during manifest lookup and chunk download phases.

**Payload:**
```ts
{ progress: number }
```

**Example:**
```js
nex.on("progress", (data) => {
  console.log(`Loading: ${data.progress}%`)
})
```

items.label: ready
items.content:
# `ready` Event

Fired when the entire HTML payload has been successfully fetched, validated, merged, and cached. The game is now primed for execution.

**Payload:** `void`

**Example:**
```js
nex.on("ready", () => {
  console.log("Game is ready to start!")
  nex.start()
})
```

items.label: error
items.content:
# `error` Event

Fired when a network failure occurs, the validator rejects a payload, or the alias does not exist.

**Payload:**
```ts
{ message: string }
```

**Example:**
```js
nex.on("error", (err) => {
  console.error("Game loading failed:", err.message)
})
```

items.label: Race Fetch Strategy
Cache-First Strategy
items.content:
# Aggressive Cache-First Strategy

All network requests check the `np-cache-1` Cache Storage API before hitting the network, eliminating repetitive data consumption over mobile/4G networks.

**Benefits:**
- Reduces bandwidth usage
- Faster subsequent loads
- Works offline after first load

**Example:**
```js
// Internal caching mechanism
const cache = await caches.open('np-cache-1')
const cached = await cache.match(request)
if (cached) return cached
const response = await fetch(request)
cache.put(request, response.clone())
return response
```

items.label: Self-Healing Runtime
items.content:
# Self-Healing Runtime

Listens to live attribute alterations (`alias`, `gid`) via `attributeChangedCallback`, gracefully terminating active streams, clearing event registries, and hot-reloading new game pipelines without layout shifting.

**Supported mutations:**
- `alias` change → reloads new game
- `gid` change → creates new instance context

**Benefits:**
- No page refresh required
- State cleanup prevents memory leaks
- Smooth transitions between games

items.label: Sandbox Iframe
items.content:
# Unrestricted Sandbox Iframe

Injects the game into an isolated Shadow DOM container with maximized permissions allowed for feature policy capabilities.

**Enabled features:**
- Pointer lock
- Local storage
- Audio autoplay
- Gamepad API

**Implementation:**
```html
<iframe
  sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-pointer-lock allow-autoplay allow-modals"
  allow="autoplay; gamepad; pointer-lock"
>
</iframe>
```

**Security note:** The sandbox provides isolation while allowing necessary permissions for game functionality.

items.label: Basic Usage
items.content:
# Basic Usage Example

Complete example of loading and starting a game with the NexGame component.

## HTML
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/usenex/nex-js@f10e7a480b7d1d3b5af4b0e3066d8115f7f0c356/nex.min.js"></script>
</head>
<body>
  <nex-game alias="fnaf" gid="my-game-1"></nex-game>

  <script>
    const gid = "my-game-1"
    
    window.nex[gid].on("progress", (data) => {
      console.log(`Loading progress: ${data.progress}%`)
    })

    window.nex[gid].on("ready", () => {
      console.log("Game ready!")
      window.nex[gid].start()
    })

    window.nex[gid].on("error", (err) => {
      console.error("Game error:", err.message)
    })
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```
